item.text: The ACT Integrity Commission investigated whether Education Directorate officials acted honestly and impartially during the 2019–2020 procurement for the Campbell Primary School Modernisation Project.
item.support:
into whether public officials in the ACT Education 
Directorate (EDU) failed to exercise their official functions honestly and or impartially

item.text: It examined the selection of Lendlease despite evaluation teams favouring Manteena, including communications involving ministerial staff, union officials and public servants.
item.support:
involved communications between the Minister’s office, 
union officials, persons within EDU and the Directorate tasked with delivery of the 
Project

item.text: The Commission found that the then director-general and the minister's chief of staff engaged in serious corrupt conduct by improperly influencing the procurement and trying to conceal what occurred.
item.support:
Accordingly, the corrupt conduct of each 
amounted to serious corrupt conduct.

item.text: The Commission declined to find that another official engaged in serious corrupt conduct, taking account of his later disclosures and efforts to correct the wrongdoing.
item.support:

that it is not appropriate to find that Mr Green’s conduct, considered as a whole, 
amounted to serious corrupt conduct.
